app_note: Re-check in January 2027 when new HHS guidelines are published
effective_date_note: Federal Register: 'Effective Date: January 13, 2026 unless an office administering a program using the guidelines specifies a different effective date for that particular program.'
source_title: Annual Update of the HHS Poverty Guidelines (Federal Register notice, 91 FR 1797, FR Doc. 2026-00755, published 2026-01-15); also ASPE 'Poverty Guidelines' page (HHS Poverty Guidelines for 2026)
notes: Only fpl_100_annual values and the per-additional-person $5,680 are as stated by the source. fpl_200_* and monthly values are computed by LeasePath tooling: 200% = 2 x 100% annual; monthly = annual/12, rounded to nearest dollar (half up), exact value also shown.

Figures read directly from the Federal Register notice text (govinfo.gov) and the ASPE poverty-guidelines page; both agree. The ASPE 2026 multiples chart PDF (detailed-guidelines-2026.pdf) lists 200% annual values identical to the computed fpl_200_annual (31,920 ... 111,440) and 100% monthly values to the cent.
Alaska and Hawaii have separate, higher tables; not recorded here. New York and DC use the 48 contiguous states and DC table.

The Federal Register effective date (2026-01-13) applies 'unless an office administering a program using the guidelines specifies a different effective date for that particular program.' HRA/DSS have not been found to state a program-specific effective date.

ASPE page notes the 2026 calculation compared the average CPI-U for 11 available months of 2025 (October excluded due to the federal shutdown) with all 12 months of 2024; the notice states a 2.63 percent price increase.
HRA HASA FAQ SPSVC-18 (E) 06/12/2026 uses '200% x $15,960 FPL = $31,920' in an example, consistent with these 2026 figures.
Retrieved 2026-10-18 via curl/WebFetch/WebSearch. Federal Register govinfo HTML was fetched directly; the federalregister.gov web page was seen via search result only.
monthly_note: fpl_200_monthly is rounded to the nearest dollar and overstates the limit for sizes 2, 5 and 8. Compare income in annual dollars (monthly x 12) against fpl_200_annual. If a monthly figure is shown, use fpl_200_monthly_floor ('or less'). Corrected 2026-10-18.
recheck: New HHS guidelines expected around January 2027; re-check then.
